open_points.subject: A07 proof-time disclosure propagation through guards
open_points.text: “the class that can reach any of its inputs”
open_points.question: Does proof compute the maximum class over every structurally possible source without considering guard correlations, or may mutually exclusive guard values narrow the class that can reach a function in one execution?
options: Ignore guard correlations and take the maximum over all possible incoming sources
Use guard correlations to compute a separate reachable class for each guard outcome
open_points.default_guess: Ignore guard correlations and conservatively take the maximum over all possible incoming sources.

open_points.subject: A07 execution class with no inputs or outputs
open_points.text: “The class of an execution is the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs … and for an operation also among its outputs”
open_points.question: What class does an execution have when that set is empty, especially an inputless function failure or an operation with neither inputs nor outputs?
options: Treat the empty maximum as open
Leave the class absent
Derive it from the node or binding by another rule
open_points.default_guess: Treat the empty maximum as open.

open_points.subject: A07 redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: “returned to an agent only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: Is length the UTF-8 byte length or character count, and is it the length of the stored truncated detail or of the original detail before truncation?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Character count of the stored bounded detail
Original pre-truncation length
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail.

open_points.subject: Mapped operation over an empty list
open_points.text: A07 says “A binding output … takes the class the binding declares … for the empty lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike”, while A13 says “an empty list takes the highest class among the node's inputs”
open_points.question: Which disclosure class must an empty output list of a mapped operation carry?
options: The binding output port's declared class
The highest class among the mapped operation's inputs
open_points.default_guess: Use the binding output port's declared class because A07 states an explicit operation-output exception.

open_points.subject: A17 credential trailing newline
open_points.text: “its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value”
open_points.question: What exactly counts as the one removable newline: LF only, CRLF as one newline, or any Unicode newline, and are additional trailing newlines rejected or left for the control-character check?
options: Remove one final LF only
Remove one final LF or CRLF sequence
Remove one final Unicode newline sequence
open_points.default_guess: Remove one final LF, also removing a preceding CR as part of CRLF, and then apply the remaining validation.

open_points.subject: A17 credential control characters
open_points.text: “holds an empty value or a control character”
open_points.question: Which characters are control characters for credential validation: ASCII C0 and DEL, all Unicode General Category Cc characters, or another HTTP-specific set?
options: ASCII C0 characters and DEL
Every Unicode Cc character
The HTTP field-value forbidden-character set
open_points.default_guess: Refuse ASCII C0 characters and DEL.

open_points.subject: A17 non-ASCII credential values
open_points.text: “its content decoded as UTF-8 … is the value” and “A resolved value is added as that header”
open_points.question: If the decoded credential contains non-ASCII characters, what bytes are sent in the HTTP header, or must such a credential be refused?
options: Require the credential value to be ASCII
Encode the value as UTF-8 header bytes
Use an HTTP-library-specific header encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require an ASCII credential value and report credential_unresolved otherwise.

open_points.subject: A17 selected instance name absent from the manifest
open_points.text: “service_instances: at most one selected instance per service, by its manifest instance name”
open_points.question: What happens when configuration selects a non-existent instance name: does the kernel refuse to start, treat the service as having no selected instance, or treat it as an instance with a missing address when proposing or invoking a binding?
options: Refuse kernel startup
Treat the service as having no selected instance
Report instance_address_missing when the service is used
open_points.default_guess: Treat the service as having no selected instance and refuse proposals or sends for that service.

open_points.subject: Configuration security after startup
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file to be regular, non-symlink, owner-owned and inaccessible to group or others, while A16 says “Exactly four checks apply to a re-read” and “Every other field of the configuration, and every other start check, applies only at a restart”
open_points.question: If the configuration file is replaced after startup by a symlink, a file owned by another user, or a group-readable file, must token re-reading reject every request or accept the new token list after only A16's four checks?
options: Repeat A17's secure-open, ownership and mode checks on every re-read
Apply only A16's four re-read checks after startup
Secure-open without following links but do not recheck ownership or mode
open_points.default_guess: Repeat the secure-open, ownership and mode checks on every configuration re-read.

open_points.subject: A13 scheduler eligibility
open_points.text: “The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id … a node is ready when every input port holds its value”
open_points.question: How are already-concluded nodes and nodes whose remaining elements are all waiting excluded from selection, since their input ports still hold values and the stated readiness test would select them repeatedly?
options: Ready also requires at least one executable unconcluded, non-waiting element and no final node conclusion
Keep the stated readiness definition but separately mark selected nodes as completed or blocked
Allow repeated selection that performs no work until a separate fixed-point check stops it
open_points.default_guess: A node is schedulable only if it is not finally concluded and has at least one unconcluded element that is not waiting.

open_points.subject: Retries after a recorded waiting attempt
open_points.text: A13 says “a concluded element is never executed again”, while A09 records service_unreachable as a NodeExecution, A14 resends that element on resume, and A11 resends after an outcome_unknown attempt is resolved not_applied
open_points.question: Does “concluded element” mean any element having a NodeExecution, or only an element whose latest attempt has a terminal conclusion rather than a retryable wait?
options: Only a terminally concluded element is never executed again
Any NodeExecution permanently prevents another attempt
Service-unreachable and not-applied retries are explicit exceptions
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as terminal conclusion only; retryable waits may create later numbered NodeExecutions.

open_points.subject: A13 ordering of newly non-executable nodes
open_points.text: “A node an input of which comes from a failed node … concludes upstream_failed” and “An input port that can no longer receive a value … makes its node skipped_by_guard”
open_points.question: When a completed node simultaneously makes downstream nodes skipped or upstream_failed while independent nodes are ready, are all derived conclusion records written immediately before another executable node is selected, or are derived conclusions interleaved with executable nodes by node_id?
options: Write the full transitive wave of derived conclusions immediately, ordered as A15 states
Choose between executable and derived-conclusion nodes together by node_id
Execute all currently ready nodes before deriving skips and upstream failures
open_points.default_guess: Write the full transitive wave of derived conclusions immediately, using A15's ordering, then select the next executable node.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped-node aggregate failure status
open_points.text: “a list whose canonical bytes exceed stored_value_bytes_max … the node is then failed … No record of the node states that failure”
open_points.question: What exact durable fact lets every reader distinguish this aggregate-size failure from other mapped-node failures and report its reason after release or restart, given that no NodeExecution records it?
options: Derive it solely by reconstructing every delivered output list and comparing its size to the current release ceiling
Persist a separate aggregate-failure fact
Write a node-level NodeExecution for the aggregate failure
open_points.default_guess: Derive it from the element records and the ceiling that applied to the run, but that applicable ceiling must be durably identifiable.

open_points.subject: Mapped aggregate failure across releases
open_points.text: A13 says the failure is “derived from the elements' records and stored_value_bytes_max, the same way by every reader of the trace”, while A20 permits a new release to change ceilings
open_points.question: Which release's stored_value_bytes_max is used to re-derive an old mapped node's aggregate failure after an upgrade, since the run records do not name a release or ceiling and recorded executions must not be reinterpreted?
options: Persist or otherwise pin the ceiling used by the run
Always use the current release ceiling
Treat the aggregate-size result as a recorded fact despite saying no record states it
open_points.default_guess: Pin the release or exact stored_value_bytes_max used by the run so later readers reproduce the original result.
